title: The Third Derivative: Jerk
teaches: The third derivative represents jerk—the rate of change of acceleration.
visual: A third graph appears below the second. The green f''(t) curve is now differentiated to create a red curve, f'''(t). A slider moves along the time axis; when the green line (acceleration) rises sharply, the red line (jerk) spikes upward. Labels 'Jerk' and 'f'''(t)' are highlighted.
narration: But acceleration doesn't change smoothly in real life. The third derivative, known as jerk, measures how abruptly acceleration changes. High jerk means a sudden, jarring shift in force.

title: Generalization: Higher Orders
teaches: Higher-order derivatives continue this pattern, describing the rate of change of the previous derivative.
visual: A stack of graphs builds up: f(t), f'(t), f''(t), f'''(t), and then a dashed curve for f^(4)(t). Each step shows an arrow labeled 'd/dt' pointing to the next. The sequence fades into a general formula notation: d^n/dx^n. Text appears: 'Mathematical Abstraction'.
narration: We can continue this process indefinitely. Each higher-order derivative describes how the previous rate of change is evolving. While physical interpretations become abstract, the mathematical pattern remains consistent: differentiation applied repeatedly.
